basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Separates the description of an action from the permission to perform it: a defined action grants nothing by itself.
Keeps the requested intent immutable and digest-bound, so a retry can be proven to be the same request.
Records execution as a bounded local history with receipts, unlike a workflow engine that runs the action.
Treats compensation as a new request with its own key, never as an undo of a committed effect.

may: Draft an action request with actor, principal, resource revision, purpose and audience filled from verified context.
Retry a request with the same intent and idempotency key after continuity is established.
Cancel or let expire a request that is still pending.
Return retained evidence of a past execution to a caller allowed to read it.
mustNot: Treat an action definition, a role name or a neighbouring model as permission to act.
Fill a missing actor, principal, purpose or resource revision by guessing.
Reapply an old effect when asked for evidence, or claim an undo after commit.
Combine partial grants from different rules into one permission.
Produce external side effects through the local adapter; those need their own contract.
requiresHuman: Granting submit permission for a proposed action.
Approving compensation for a committed effect.
Resolving a request whose context no longer matches the original intent.

considerations: An agent acting for a person can cause harm in that person's name; the principal must be explicit and verifiable.
Denied reads must return a uniform withheld response so the record does not leak who asked for what.
Execution history is evidence about people's decisions and must not be rewritten to hide responsibility.
affectedParties: Principals on whose behalf actions are requested
People affected by the executed action
Operators accountable for the host system

owners.steward: The host operator of the Company Dimension holds authority over admission and execution; the action definition belongs to the owner of the domain process it describes.
masterSystems: Host identity and access management for actors and principals
Domain system of record for the resource being acted upon

items: Action definition ID and version, immutable once published.
Request ID bound to a client intent digest and an idempotency key.
Server admission ID bound once at admission, kept outside the client digest.

properties.reason: Institutional or informational subject: it has no physical body to measure.

items: An action request names an actor, a principal, a target resource revision, a purpose and an idempotency key.
It is confused with a task (a unit of work) and with an audit log entry (a record after the fact).
Duplicate execution when a retry is not recognised as the same intent.
Privilege escalation when a description is read as a grant.
Stale execution when inputs changed between request and effect.
Idempotency-key practice of HTTP APIs (IETF draft Idempotency-Key header).
Used inside a Company Dimension where a host system authenticates actors and enforces permissions.

sections.whatItIs: A companion contract for a Company Dimension that records governed actions: what an action is, who asked for it on whose behalf, under which authority, and what local execution happened, with immutable intent and receipts. It describes and validates; it does not run external side effects.
